q: מה מאפיין את הזדקנות העור בנשים קשישות ?
o: בנשים עם עור כהה יש סיכון מוגבר ליובש וירידה בקולגן
איבוד הקולגן הוא משמעותי ב- 5 השנים לאחר המנופאוזה
hypoandrogenism
עליה ברמות אלסטין ובפעילות בלוטות הזיעה
explanation:
Dermal collagen gives skin tensile strength, and estrogen helps maintain it. **Collagen loss is especially rapid during the first five years after menopause**, which separates this hormonal change from decades of sun exposure.

**A. Dark skin confers greater risk.** Pigmentation affords some protection against ultraviolet damage. Skin color alone does not predict greater menopausal collagen loss.
**B. Marked loss in the first five years.** The abrupt fall in estrogen accelerates dermal collagen loss early after menopause.
**C. Hypoandrogenism.** Estrogen deficiency is the relevant hormonal change. Androgen effects may become relatively more prominent as estrogen falls.
**D. Increased elastin and sweating.** Elastic fibers degenerate with aging. Increased functional elastin would predict better recoil, opposite to the clinical change.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 513, 1456. Kamp et al., Menopause, skin and common dermatoses, part 2, 2022, pp. 2117–2122.
explanationReviewNote: The source supports a role for estrogen in skin integrity; reaching significant collagen loss in the first five years after menopause also requires that specific time course, which it does not state.

q: אישה בת 79 עם פרקינסון מתקשה לבצע בפועל את ניהול התרופות, אך מסוגלת להבין ולקבל החלטות לגבי הטיפול. בתה מוכנה ומסוגלת לסייע לה והיא מעוניינת בכך. איזו גישה מתאימה לסעיף 33א לחוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות?
o: למנות אפוטרופוס לעניינים רפואיים.
להציע עזרה מעשית תוך שמירת ההחלטות בידיה.
לבקש צו זמני לניהול משטר התרופות שלה.
להעביר לאפוטרופוס את כלל ענייניה האישיים.
explanation:
קושי לבצע משטר תרופות שונה מקושי להחליט אם לקבל טיפול. בודקים אם תמיכה מעשית תשיג את המטרה תוך שמירה על הבחירה. **להסדיר סיוע בביצוע משטר התרופות תוך שמירת ההחלטות בידי המטופלת**.

**א. למנות אפוטרופוס לעניינים רפואיים** — אין הצדקה להעביר סמכות רפואית בגלל קושי בביצוע בלבד.
**ב. להציע עזרה מעשית תוך שמירת ההחלטות בידיה** — ארגון תרופות ותזכורות יכולים לצמצם את הסיכון בהסכמת המטופל.
**ג. לבקש צו זמני לניהול משטר התרופות שלה** — גם מינוי זמני דורש הצדקה.
**ד. להעביר לאפוטרופוס את כלל ענייניה האישיים** — מינוי בעניינים אישיים רחב מהצורך המתואר.

אסמכתא · חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיף 33א(ב), עמ׳ 45 בקובץ.

q: A 75-year-old woman receiving palliative care for advanced pancreatic cancer wishes to remain intimate with her husband. She had estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer ten years ago and now has severe dyspareunia from vaginal atrophy. Long-acting morphine controls her other pain. Which approach best reflects Hazzard's discussion of sexuality in palliative care?
o: Defer sexual-symptom assessment until the cancer treatment course is finished
Choose systemic hormone therapy before reviewing her cancer history and preferences
Discuss sexual goals and individualize relief of dyspareunia with oncology input
Focus symptom care on nonsexual concerns until the patient stops cancer treatment
explanation:
Intimacy can remain an important palliative-care goal. **Ask what intimacy she wants and tailor treatment of dyspareunia**, involving oncology when considering hormonal treatment after estrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer.

**A. Defer until cancer treatment ends.** Pain during intimacy is affecting quality of life now.
**B. Start systemic hormones immediately.** Her hormone-sensitive cancer history and preferences require review before considering estrogen.
**C. Individualize relief.** Discuss nonhormonal measures and what she finds acceptable, coordinating further treatment with her oncology team.
**D. Limit care to other symptoms.** Control of other pain does not meet her separate goal of comfortable intimacy.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 506, 534.
ref: Hazzard Ch 35 — SEXUALITY, SEXUAL FUNCTION, AND THE AGING WOMAN
chapterTitle: Sexuality, Sexual Function, and the Aging Woman

q: אישה בת 73 עם קושי קוגניטיבי קל יכולה לקבל החלטות בעזרת הסבר מותאם. מונה לה תומך בענייניה האישיים, והיא מתלבטת לגבי פעילות פנאי ויחסים חברתיים. מה תפקידו לפי מדריך קבלת החלטות נתמכת?
o: לבחור עבורה את האפשרות המתאימה לפי העדפותיו האישיות
לבקש מילדיה לבחור עבורה את האפשרות המקובלת עליהם
להנגיש חלופות ולהשאיר בידיה את בחירת האפשרות המתאימה
לכוון לאפשרות המועדפת עליו ולהציג לה את יתרונותיה בלבד
explanation:
תמיכה בקבלת החלטות מסייעת לאדם להבין, לשקול ולממש בחירה משלו, לרבות בחיי החברה והפנאי. **להנגיש חלופות ולהשאיר בידיה את בחירת האפשרות המתאימה**.

**א. לבחור עבורה את האפשרות המתאימה לפי העדפותיו האישיות.** הטעם האישי של התומך אינו שיקול מכריע.
**ב. לבקש מילדיה לבחור עבורה את האפשרות המקובלת עליהם.** הילדים יכולים לסייע אך אין להפקיד בידיהם את הבחירה.
**ג. להנגיש חלופות ולהשאיר בידיה את בחירת האפשרות המתאימה.** הנגשת החלופות מאפשרת לה להכריע.
**ד. לכוון לאפשרות המועדפת עליו ולהציג לה את יתרונותיה בלבד.** הצגת היתרונות של אפשרות אחת בלבד מכוונת את ההחלטה.

q: A 72-year-old man reports worsening urinary frequency, nocturia four to five times nightly, and a weak stream for six months. His AUASI is 18. He has hypertension, diabetes, and recent falls, takes metformin, lisinopril, and atorvastatin, and lives alone. Which drug treats BPH-related lower urinary tract symptoms through selective alpha-1A blockade?
o: Treatment with tamsulosin
Treatment with finasteride
Treatment with dutasteride
Treatment with tadalafil
explanation:
Alpha-1A receptors help maintain smooth muscle tone in the prostate and bladder outlet. **Tamsulosin blocks these receptors and can improve the weak stream.** His recent falls make postural dizziness especially important to monitor.

**A. Tamsulosin** — Relaxing outlet smooth muscle reduces resistance to flow. Urinary symptoms generally begin to improve within two to four weeks.
**B. Finasteride** — This drug lowers dihydrotestosterone production and gradually shrinks the prostate. It works over months.
**C. Dutasteride** — This is another 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor. Its target is an enzyme involved in prostate growth.
**D. Tadalafil** — This phosphodiesterase type 5 inhibitor can improve urinary symptoms through a different signaling pathway.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 565–567, Table 38-7 and Medical Therapy.

q: אישה עם סרטן מתקדם הוגדרה כחולה הנוטה למות. היא מבקשת טיפול המקל על כאב ועל סבל. מה נדרש לפי סעיף 23 לחוק החולה הנוטה למות?
o: לדחות הקלה תרופתית עד שיוסכם על מסגרת הוספיס
להעדיף טיפול בגידול על פני הקלת כאב וסבל
להימנע מהקלה כאשר היא כרוכה בסיכון סביר לחיים
להקל על כאב וסבל לפי רצונה ועקרונות הטיפול
explanation:
הקלה על סבל היא חלק מהטיפול בחולה הנוטה למות בכל מסגרת. בוחרים התערבות מקצועית המתאימה לרצונו ולתסמיניו. **להקל על כאב וסבל לפי רצונה ועקרונות הטיפול**.

**א. לדחות הקלה תרופתית עד שיוסכם על מסגרת הוספיס.** אין להמתין להשמה בהוספיס כדי לטפל בכאב.
**ב. להעדיף טיפול בגידול על פני הקלת כאב וסבל.** טיפול בגידול אינו מחליף טיפול תסמיני.
**ג. להימנע מהקלה כאשר היא כרוכה בסיכון סביר לחיים.** סיכון סביר אינו איסור על טיפול מקל.
**ד. להקל על כאב וסבל לפי רצונה ועקרונות הטיפול.** מתאימים את הטיפול לעוצמת הסבל ומעריכים שוב את השפעתו.

אסמכתא · חוק החולה הנוטה למות, תשס״ו-2005, עמ׳ 12.

q: A 79-year-old woman has functional decline, cognitive complaints, and significant depressive symptoms after a mild head injury. Which principle should guide assessment and treatment?
o: Integrate depression assessment with cognition and function in this complex presentation
Attribute functional decline to the injury and assess depression after rehabilitation
Attribute cognitive decline to the injury and assess mood on a separate pathway
Focus assessment on memory and postpone review of daily functional decline
explanation:
Depression after an injury can affect attention, activity and rehabilitation, while loss of function can worsen mood. More than one process can contribute to a change in memory or daily activities.
**Assess mood, cognition and function together, using the time course and collateral history to guide treatment.**

**A. Integrated assessment.** Determine what changed after the injury, how mood and concentration affect daily tasks, and which deficits persist when engagement improves.
**B. Wait until rehabilitation ends.** Untreated depression can itself limit participation during rehabilitation.
**C. Separate the cognitive and mood assessments.** Assuming an injury explains all cognitive symptoms misses the interaction between mood, cognition and function.
**D. Test memory and postpone functional review.** Everyday activities establish the practical impact and help distinguish impaired capacity from loss of motivation.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1008–1009, 1014, 1018–1019

q: A 78-year-old man with typical atrial flutter is being considered for catheter ablation. Which structure is the critical conduction pathway in the typical flutter circuit described by Hazzard?
o: The tissue surrounding the pulmonary vein openings in the posterior left atrium.
The region between the sinus node and the superior vena cava.
The isthmus between the inferior vena cava and the tricuspid valve.
The tissue between the conduction bundle and the left ventricular apex.
explanation:
Typical atrial flutter is a reentrant atrial rhythm with a critical right atrial passage. **The cavotricuspid isthmus lies between the inferior vena cava and tricuspid annulus.** Blocking conduction across it interrupts the circuit.

**A. Pulmonary vein openings** — These are left atrial ablation targets in atrial fibrillation.
**B. Sinus node to superior vena cava** — This superior right atrial region does not form the narrow isthmus of typical flutter.
**C. Inferior vena cava to tricuspid valve** — This is the cavotricuspid isthmus traversed by the usual flutter wavefront.
**D. Conduction bundle to ventricular apex** — Ventricular conduction tissue is outside the atrial flutter circuit.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1205–1206, Atrial Flutter.

. Sinus node to superior vena cava** — This superior right atrial region does not form the narrow isthmus of typical flutter.
. Inferior vena cava to tricuspid valve** — This is the cavotricuspid isthmus traversed by the usual flutter wavefront.
. Conduction bundle to ventricular apex** — Ventricular conduction tissue is outside the atrial flutter circuit.

q: A 78-year-old man with limited-stage small-cell lung cancer completed concurrent chemoradiation 3 months ago. He had an excellent response, with dose reductions for neutropenia. He remains independent, but his daughter reports new forgetfulness. Creatinine clearance is 40 mL/min and the latest brain MRI is normal. During discussion of prophylactic cranial irradiation, which potential treatment effect warrants attention according to Hazzard?
o: Earlier brain metastases, with increased risk following prophylactic cranial irradiation.
Late neurocognitive effects, with particular concern about preexisting cognitive impairment.
Improved cognitive function, with lower risk after whole-brain radiation therapy.
Fewer treatment-related adverse events, with lower risk among older recipients.
explanation:
Prophylactic cranial irradiation can reduce brain metastases after a small-cell lung cancer response, but **late neurocognitive toxicity deserves particular attention when baseline cognition is impaired**.

**A. Earlier brain metastases.** The intervention is intended to reduce or delay intracranial metastases.
**B. Late cognitive effects.** Baseline forgetfulness and age influence the benefit-harm discussion. Assess cognition and consider surveillance alternatives.
**C. Cognitive improvement from whole-brain irradiation.** Radiation is not a treatment for preexisting memory impairment.
**D. Fewer adverse effects with age.** Older patients may have less neurologic reserve and greater vulnerability.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, Ch 91, p. 1432.

. Late cognitive effects.** Baseline forgetfulness and age influence the benefit-harm discussion. Assess cognition and consider surveillance alternatives.
. Cognitive improvement from whole-brain irradiation.** Radiation is not a treatment for preexisting memory impairment.
. Fewer adverse effects with age.** Older patients may have less neurologic reserve and greater vulnerability.

q: A 73-year-old woman taking warfarin starts using ginkgo biloba extract. Which interaction is described in Hazzard?
o: A lower bleeding risk when ginkgo is combined with warfarin
A lower drug-interaction risk when herbal medicines are added
A higher bleeding risk when ginkgo is combined with warfarin
A lower adverse-event risk when herbal use is left unreviewed
explanation:
Warfarin inhibits coagulation, and ginkgo constituents may inhibit platelet activation or aggregation. **Ginkgo taken with warfarin can add bleeding risk**, although the size and consistency of that interaction are not firmly established. Ask about the specific preparation, timing and bleeding symptoms.

**A. Lower bleeding risk.** A potential antiplatelet effect acts in the same hazardous direction as anticoagulation for bleeding, rather than protecting against it.
**B. Herbal medicines lower interaction risk.** Supplement ingredients and doses vary and can add interactions even when prescribed drug doses have not changed.
**C. Higher bleeding risk.** Bleeding has been reported with combined use, including an association in observational data. This supports reviewing the combination without predicting an exact risk for this woman.
**D. Leave supplements unreviewed.** An incomplete medication list can conceal contributors to bruising or hemorrhage; a normal INR would not measure a potential platelet effect.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 302. Ginkgo and Warfarin Interaction in a Large Veterans Administration Population, PMCID PMC4765589.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

. Higher bleeding risk.** Bleeding has been reported with combined use, including an association in observational data. This supports reviewing the combination without predicting an exact risk for this woman.
. Leave supplements unreviewed.** An incomplete medication list can conceal contributors to bruising or hemorrhage; a normal INR would not measure a potential platelet effect.

q: באיזה מהמקרים הבאים יתכן ויהיה צורך בהעלאת מינון LEVOTHYROXINE בשל הפרעות בספיגתו?
o: התחלת טיפול ב- CARBAMAZEPINE בשל אירוע פרכוסי
תוספת טיפול בסידן CALCIUM CARBONATE בשל אוסטאופורוזיס
תוספת טיפול בברזל פומי בשל אנמיה
תוספת טיפול ב- ESOMEPRAZOLE בשל גסטריטיס
explanation:
An oral levothyroxine dose may need adjustment when less drug reaches the circulation or when the body clears it faster. **All four drugs can increase the dose requirement. Calcium carbonate, iron and esomeprazole can impair absorption, while carbamazepine accelerates metabolism.**

**A. Carbamazepine** Hepatic enzyme induction increases levothyroxine metabolism. More hormone may be needed even though intestinal absorption is not the mechanism.
**B. Calcium carbonate** Calcium can bind levothyroxine in the gut, leaving less available for absorption.
**C. Oral iron** Iron supplements also bind levothyroxine in the gastrointestinal tract, particularly when taken together.
**D. Esomeprazole** Proton pump inhibition reduces gastric acidity and may decrease absorption of levothyroxine tablets.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, p. 1553, Table 98-7.

Key note: All four choices are accepted. Table 98-7 places carbamazepine under increased metabolism, whereas the question specifically asks about impaired absorption.

q: Must a patient stop curative treatment to receive palliative care?
o: Yes; palliative care generally begins after disease-directed therapy has been abandoned
Yes; curative treatment usually needs to be stopped before palliative care begins
No; palliative care is compatible with continued treatment aimed at cure
No; eligibility for palliative care depends on prior enrollment in hospice
explanation:
Palliative care treats the suffering and practical problems of serious illness. It can begin while treatment still aims to cure or control the illness.
**Patients can receive palliative care while continuing curative treatment.**

**A. Begin only after abandoning disease therapy** A patient may need symptom relief from the day of diagnosis.
**B. Stop curative treatment** A team can manage treatment-related symptoms while curative treatment continues.
**C. Combine both approaches** The teams share goals and can address physical symptoms, family needs and decisions together.
**D. Enroll in hospice first** Hospice is one form of palliative care for limited prognosis. General palliative care has a wider remit.

Reference · Hazzard 8e, pp. 1045–1046.

o: היפרגליקמיה

היפרקלצמיה

keySource: IMA 2024-Sep Basic official answer key after appeals, Q104
explanation:
Tumor lysis releases intracellular solutes after effective chemotherapy. **Hyperphosphatemia** is a characteristic finding, alongside hyperkalemia and hyperuricemia. Calcium can fall as it binds phosphate.

**A. Hyperglycemia.** Elevated glucose is not a defining consequence of rapid tumor-cell lysis.
**B. Hyperphosphatemia.** Intracellular phosphate enters the bloodstream as large numbers of cells break down.
**C. Hypercalcemia.** The characteristic calcium disturbance is in the opposite direction.
**D. Hypernatremia.** Sodium elevation is not part of the typical tumor-lysis pattern.

Reference · Harrison 22e, p. 593.
